sharepoint-knowledge-agent.title: Get started with Copilot in SharePoint – Microsoft Learn
sharepoint-knowledge-agent.notes: This page covers the agent that was previewed as the Knowledge Agent and is now documented as Copilot in SharePoint; the old name survives only in PowerShell parameter names. It brings agentic abilities into SharePoint, so teams can ask questions in natural language, run workflows, and generate sites, pages, interactive reports and Office files from SharePoint content. Everyday tasks are covered by a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, while heavier work such as processing large content sets, building whole sites or running multi-step AI workflows needs usage-based billing and Copilot credits. Admins can control availability through site AI settings, Restricted Content Discovery, or a tenant-level PowerShell scope setting that is limited to a fixed period. The page states that a Microsoft-managed OpenAI reasoning model is used and needs no configuration. Limits include no availability in GCC, GCC High, DoD, air-gapped clouds and the 21Vianet-operated cloud, and support only for languages present in both the SharePoint and Copilot language lists. Without credits, advanced tasks stop and the agent explains what it could not finish.

windows-update-for-business.title: Windows Update client policies – Microsoft Learn
windows-update-for-business.notes: The page notes that this feature used to be called Windows Update for Business and is now documented as Windows Update client policies. It is a free service for Windows 10 and Windows 11 Pro, Education and Enterprise editions that connects devices directly to the Windows Update service. Its purpose is to keep devices current with security and feature updates while letting administrators decide which updates are offered and when, including testing on a subset of devices before a wider rollout. Settings are applied through Group Policy or an MDM solution such as Microsoft Intune. Administrators can defer feature updates for up to 365 days and quality updates for up to 30 days, and pause updates for 35 days. They can also set deadlines, choose a branch readiness level, and control driver and Microsoft product updates. Limits include no feature updates for LTSC devices, no support for Click-to-Run Office, and an Update Baseline that applies only to Group Policy. Windows Update for Business reports and Windows Autopatch build on these policies.

active-directory-forest.title: Understanding the Active Directory Logical Model – Microsoft Learn
active-directory-forest.notes: The page places the forest at the top of the Active Directory logical hierarchy, above domains and organizational units. A forest is a collection of one or more Active Directory domains that share a common logical structure. The domains in it also share a single directory schema, which holds the class and attribute definitions, and a common directory configuration, which covers site and replication information. They additionally share a global catalog that allows searching across the whole forest. Domains inside one forest are linked automatically by two-way transitive trusts. The page stresses that this logical model is independent of the physical deployment, such as the number of domain controllers or the network topology. It does not describe the forest as a security boundary or list numeric limits.

at-least-once-delivery.title: Prevent message loss and duplicate processing in Azure Service Bus – Microsoft Learn
at-least-once-delivery.notes: In Azure Service Bus, the peek-lock receive mode gives at-least-once delivery, meaning a message can arrive more than once but is not lost. The broker locks a message when it is received and removes it only after the consumer completes it. If processing fails or the lock expires first, the message is delivered again. Receive-and-delete mode, in contrast, offers at-most-once delivery because the message is removed immediately and can be lost on a crash. The page recommends peek lock for any workload that cannot accept message loss, and it is the default mode. Repeated deliveries can come from slow processing beyond the lock duration, dropped AMQP links, retried send or settle calls, or consumers that restart mid-processing. Recommended practice is to settle explicitly, renew locks for long work, keep prefetch modest, and make consumers idempotent, for example by using a message ID. Duplicate detection covers retried sends only within a configured time window and does not replace idempotent receivers. Messages that exceed the maximum delivery count go to a dead-letter queue.

attribute-based-access-control.title: What is Azure attribute-based access control (Azure ABAC)? – Microsoft Learn
attribute-based-access-control.notes: ABAC is described as an authorization approach that decides access using attributes of the security principal, the resource and the environment of a request. Azure ABAC builds on Azure role-based access control by adding role assignment conditions to existing role assignments. A condition is an optional extra check, written as an expression of the form attribute, operator and value, which evaluates to true or false. Attributes are key-value pairs, such as a project tag, and can come from blob storage properties, the request environment, or custom security attributes on the principal. The page lists three benefits: finer-grained access, fewer role assignments because subscriptions have an assignment limit, and use of business-related attributes. Typical examples allow reading only blobs with a certain tag or writing only through a private link. Conditions currently apply only to roles with Blob Storage or Queue Storage data actions, require permission to write role assignments, and cannot be used to explicitly deny access. The visual editor supports a limited number of expressions per condition, and the code editor allows more.

azure-cloud-shell.title: What is Azure Cloud Shell? – Microsoft Learn
azure-cloud-shell.notes: Azure Cloud Shell is an interactive, authenticated shell that runs in the browser and is used to manage Azure resources with either Bash or PowerShell. Common command-line tools and language support come preinstalled, and authentication for Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell happens automatically and securely. The shell includes a built-in graphical text editor for creating and editing files that are then deployed through the CLI or PowerShell. It can be reached from the Azure portal, shell.azure.com, the documentation pages, the Azure mobile app and the Azure Account extension for Visual Studio Code. Files in the home directory persist through an Azure Files share with a fixed size, so a storage account is required. Using the host machine is free, but regular storage charges apply. Sessions end after a period without interactive activity, the host is temporary and assigned per user and session, and the user has the rights of a regular Linux user. Data at rest is encrypted by default.

azure-integration-services.title: Azure Integration Services – Microsoft Azure
azure-integration-services.notes: Microsoft presents Azure Integration Services as an integration platform that connects applications and cloud systems, automates business processes and manages APIs. It is positioned for linking older systems with newer technologies. The collection includes Azure Logic Apps for workflows and automation, Azure API Management for publishing, securing and governing APIs in the cloud and on premises, Azure Service Bus for messaging, Azure Event Grid as a publish-subscribe service for event-driven designs, Azure Data Factory for hybrid data integration, and Azure Functions for event-driven serverless code. A large library of prebuilt connectors and templates is mentioned. API Management also offers features for AI workloads, such as token limits, token tracking, semantic caching and load balancing for large language models. Typical scenarios are cross-product process automation, decoupling services with message brokers and events, and exposing AI models behind an API gateway. The page names no concrete licensing model or technical limits and refers readers to Azure pricing pages.

azure-resource-group.title: What is Azure Resource Manager? – Microsoft Learn
azure-resource-group.notes: A resource group is a container for related resources of an Azure solution, so they can be managed together and changes can be coordinated. Resources in one group should share a lifecycle, meaning they are deployed, updated and deleted together; a resource with a different lifecycle belongs elsewhere. Each resource lives in exactly one resource group, can be added or removed at any time, and can be moved to another group or subscription. Deleting a group deletes everything inside it. Access to a group can be restricted with Azure Policy, role-based access control or resource locks. Tags set on a group are not inherited by its resources, and resources may connect to others in different groups. A location must be chosen at creation because the group stores metadata about its resources and control-plane requests are routed through that location, while data-plane access is unaffected. If the group's region is unavailable, Resource Manager redirects control-plane requests to a backup region. A group can hold a limited number of instances per resource type, with some exceptions.

border-gateway-protocol.title: About BGP with Azure VPN Gateway – Microsoft Learn
border-gateway-protocol.notes: BGP is the standard routing protocol used on the internet to exchange routing and reachability information between two or more networks. In Azure, VPN gateways and on-premises VPN devices act as BGP peers, or neighbors, and exchange routes and prefixes. It replaces static routing with dynamic routing, though using it with a VPN gateway is optional. Prefix updates happen automatically, and a peer only needs to declare a minimal prefix over the tunnel. With several active tunnels between a virtual network and an on-premises site, a failed tunnel's routes are withdrawn and traffic shifts to the remaining tunnels. Gateways can also learn prefixes from various networks and pass them on, enabling transit routing between sites or between virtual networks. BGP requires a route-based VPN gateway, and the on-premises device must support BGP. A BGP prefix may not be identical to a virtual network prefix, because such routes are rejected, although larger prefixes that contain the address space are allowed.

business-central-extensions.title: Developing extensions in AL – Microsoft Learn
business-central-extensions.notes: Extensions are the programming model for Business Central in which functionality is defined as an addition to existing objects instead of changing the base code. The model is object-based: developers create new objects or extend existing ones such as tables, pages, reports, enums and code flows. The objects are written in the AL language and stored in .al files, with one object per file recommended. Typical object types are tables for schema, pages for the user interface, codeunits for logic, and reports, plus table extensions and page extensions that add or override parts of existing objects. A .app package bundles the artifacts with a manifest holding name, publisher and version. Development uses Visual Studio Code with the AL Language extension, which offers compiler validation, snippets, IntelliSense and publishing to a tenant. Telemetry can be connected to an Azure Application Insights resource. Before submission to the marketplace, a checklist is recommended and the AppSourceCop analyzer can be enabled.

cloud-center-of-excellence.title: Cloud center of excellence (CCoE) functions – Microsoft Learn
cloud-center-of-excellence.notes: In the Cloud Adoption Framework, a cloud center of excellence is a function that helps an organization balance speed and stability to reach business and technical agility. It brings together cloud adoption, cloud strategy, cloud governance, cloud platform and cloud automation roles. Its main job is to speed up cloud adoption with cloud-native or hybrid solutions, using reusable deployment packages aligned to security, compliance and management policies. It also maintains the Azure platform, reviews and approves cloud-native tools, and over time standardizes and automates common platform components. The page describes IT shifting from operator toward broker or partner, with business units making self-service decisions within guardrails. Prerequisites include executive and business stakeholder support, documented business goals and pain points, and willingness of IT to give up some central control. Challenges named are the time needed, no guarantee of success, resistance from existing IT teams, the resource commitment, and the risk of demotivated or reassigned team members. The page presents it as one valid model, not a mandatory one.

coe-starter-kit.title: Power Platform Center of Excellence (CoE) Starter Kit overview – Microsoft Learn
coe-starter-kit.notes: The CoE Starter Kit is a reference implementation made of components and solutions for governing, monitoring and driving adoption of Power Platform with native low-code tools. It is built on Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, Dataverse and Copilot Studio, with a Dataverse data model and workflows that collect resource information from environments in the tenant. It contains several apps and Power BI reports, templates and practices for CoE tasks, and automation for monitoring. Its areas are Admin for usage insight, Govern for audit and compliance processes such as inactivity notices and a DLP editor, and Nurture for community building. Typical uses include reviewing resources and makers in a dashboard and reassigning orphaned apps. The page states that the kit is no longer actively maintained, that issues are not reviewed, and that its core capabilities now exist in the Power Platform admin center. It is sample code that may need adaptation, and it does not replace a real CoE with people and processes. The kit is downloaded from a GitHub repository.

cross-tenant-access-settings.title: Cross-tenant access settings overview – Microsoft Learn
cross-tenant-access-settings.notes: Cross-tenant access settings let an organization manage collaboration with other Microsoft Entra organizations and Azure clouds through B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect. They contain inbound and outbound controls, each applicable to all users or to chosen users, groups and applications, plus inbound trust settings that decide whether Conditional Access accepts MFA, compliant-device and hybrid-joined claims from the partner's home tenant. Default settings apply to everyone, and organization-specific settings override them for individual partners. By default B2B collaboration is on, direct connect is blocked, and claims from other organizations are not trusted. Further options include automatic redemption, configurable redemption order for identity providers, and cross-tenant synchronization controls. Trust settings and targeted rules for users, groups or apps need Microsoft Entra ID P1, and direct connect needs it in both tenants. Direct connect is not supported between clouds, and blocking default access can interrupt business-critical access, so the page advises planning with business owners first.

customer-managed-keys.title: Customer-managed keys for Azure Storage encryption – Microsoft Learn
customer-managed-keys.notes: For Azure Storage, customer-managed keys let an organization use its own encryption key to protect and control the key that in turn encrypts the data in a storage account. The key must be held in Azure Key Vault or Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, which can be in a different tenant, region or subscription than the account. A managed identity is granted permission on the key, and Azure Storage authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID, wraps the account encryption key with the customer key, and unwraps it for reads and writes. The vault needs soft delete and purge protection, and the key must be an RSA or RSA-HSM key of an allowed size. Blob Storage and Azure Files are always protected, whereas queue and table protection is optional at account creation. Rotation is the customer's job through a Key Vault policy, and Storage checks daily for new versions when no version is pinned. Disabling the key makes covered operations fail with a forbidden error for all users. Key Vault and Managed HSM carry their own costs.

data-partitioning.title: Data partitioning guidance – Azure Architecture Center
data-partitioning.notes: The guidance defines partitioning as physically dividing data into separate data stores, and distinguishes it from SQL Server table partitioning. Stated aims are scalability, performance, security, operational flexibility, matching stores to usage patterns, and availability. Three strategies are described: horizontal partitioning, or sharding, where each shard has the same schema but a subset of rows; vertical partitioning, where fields are split by usage pattern; and functional partitioning, where data is grouped by bounded context or business area. The shard key is the most important design factor and is hard to change once in operation, and balanced access matters more than equal shard sizes. Partitioning should be considered early in the design. The page names drawbacks, including slower cross-partition queries, limited cross-partition transactions that must be handled in application logic, referential integrity left to the application, eventual consistency, and complex rebalancing, backup and restore.

dataverse-plug-in.title: Plug-ins overview – Microsoft Learn (Dataverse)
dataverse-plug-in.notes: A Dataverse plug-in is a custom event handler that responds to a specific event during the processing of a data operation. It is written as a class in a .NET Framework assembly that is then registered in Dataverse, and one assembly can hold several classes registered to different steps of the event framework. Each class implements the IPlugin interface with a single Execute method, which receives context data about the operation. Plug-in code can cancel the running pipeline operation, change the business data being processed, call further data operations, contact external systems, or pass information to later plug-ins in the same pipeline. Plug-ins can run synchronously, so the operation waits for them, or asynchronously after the operation completes. The page advises checking declarative options first and lists alternatives such as custom actions, calculated and rollup columns, webhooks and Power Automate. Drawbacks are the need for developer skills, a possible hit to performance if code is poorly written, the need for synchronous plug-ins to run quickly, and a hard time limit on execution.
